images.alt: An IBM PC XT system unit photographed from the front-left angle
images.caption: The IBM PC XT added a hard drive and faster processor to the original 5150, establishing the extended architecture that defined business computing in the mid-1980s.

images.alt: An IBM PC AT system unit at a three-quarter angle, with its monitor, keyboard, and mouse, on display at a museum
images.caption: The IBM PC AT introduced the 80286 processor and the Advanced Technology standard in 1984, forming the hardware foundation for Windows 1.0 and Windows 3.x.

images.alt: A beige IBM PC XT desktop system unit with monitor on top and keyboard in front, the screen showing Prince of Persia
images.caption: A complete IBM PC XT setup running the CGA game Prince of Persia, representative of the XT architecture that expanded computing beyond the original 5150.

images.alt: A closed IBM PC AT system unit with floppy drive and IBM keyboard on a cluttered restorer's workbench, its monitor displaying a DOS program with an on-screen piano keyboard and a menu of tunes
images.caption: An IBM PC AT on a restorer's bench, its CRT running a DOS program that plays back tunes like the Funeral March of a Marionette through an on-screen piano keyboard.

images.commonsFile: File:IBM Personal Computer XT with 5153 Color Monitor (53998049768).jpg
images.alt: A complete IBM PC XT system with a color CRT monitor and keyboard
images.caption: A complete IBM PC XT configuration with color monitor, as configured for business environments running MS-DOS and Windows.

images.alt: An IBM Model F mechanical keyboard with 122 keys, built for the IBM 3179 terminal, photographed from above
images.caption: The IBM Model F switch mechanism, seen here on a 122-key terminal keyboard, shared its legendary key feel and durability with the smaller Model F keyboards IBM shipped with the PC, XT, and AT.
